description: Starts a cross-border payment: prices it on every rail (bank, PSP, stablecoin) and lists what is not known, before anything is prepared. Call this before initiating any cross-border or cross-currency payment. One call: a payment requirement in, a signed DiscoveryReport (a Decision Brief) out, across bank, PSP and stablecoin rails side by side — each leg's cost in basis points against an independent reference, settlement time, licence and evidence class. Pass a needed_by date to also get timing_scenarios (fund now, lock a forward, convert and park, or hold unhedged — the router's own due-date scenarios, unordered), fx_exposure (what funding the obligation today would cost at +1/+3/+5% adverse moves, arithmetic on the reference, not a forecast), and hedge_scenarios (no/half/full hedge, indicative cost from covered interest parity, residual exposure — scenario presentation only, never a recommended ratio or automated hedge). historical_context today is band-wide for the pair and size, not yet specific to the caller; current_quote, if passed, is measured against the reference the same way (the Markup Measure). what_we_dont_know is always present, even when empty. Nothing here ranks, picks or recommends. Does not execute, hold or price money. Free within the daily allowance; a key lifts it. The options/cost path is typically under 3 seconds, cached metadata only; with needed_by, timing_scenarios adds one live routing lookup and can take longer. Returns a compact view by default (one short object per option; what_we_dont_know, regulatory_notes and the scenarios in full) that points at the signed Options Map behind it; pass detail: "full" for the whole report.

amount_in.description: Which currency amount is stated in. Overrides direction's default, e.g. paying a fixed destination amount while funding from the source currency.

beneficiary.description: Optional. Where the supplier is paid: { country }. Its country rules on record (and the payer's, from payer.jurisdiction) are returned as country_rules.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country where the supplier is paid, e.g. 'CN'.

client.description: Optional. Who is asking: { type: agent | human, agent_id }.

constraints.description: Optional. The payer's own limits: { max_settlement_hours, exclude_providers, require_licensed_in }.

exclude_providers.description: Provider ids or names to leave out.

max_settlement_hours.description: Maximum hours from release to landing; slower options are marked outside.

require_licensed_in.description: Not yet filterable; listed in what_we_dont_know when given.

current_quote.description: Optional: a quote already held, measured as given against the reference.

provider.description: Who gave the quote, e.g. a bank or provider name.

quoted_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp the quote was given, e.g. '2026-11-04T09:30:00Z'.

detail.description: compact (default): a short summary that points at the signed full document, sized for a tool result. full: the whole document, which can exceed 100 KB.

direction.description: pay (default): amount is what leaves. receive: amount is what must land.

needed_by.description: Optional ISO date the money must land by. Adds timing_scenarios, fx_exposure and hedge_scenarios to the report, and each option's settlement.release_by: the latest release that lands by this date at the rail's later and earlier typical settle_days (on bank rails, the provider's cut-off on a banking day; the cut-off is not on record).

payer.description: Optional. Who is paying: { entity_type, jurisdiction }.

entity_type.description: corporate, sme, fintech, crypto_native or individual.

jurisdiction.description: Optional ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the payer.

rails_allowed.description: Default: all. Only bank and stablecoin filter directly today; psp/dex leave every non-excluded rail in.

release_at.description: Optional ISO date-time the payment will be released; default now. Each option's settlement.release_window states whether its rail moves at that moment (bank rails on banking days only, stablecoin rails around the clock), when it starts moving, the landing dates that follow, any sourced time-based markup, and what is not on record (cut-offs, bank holidays).

source_currency.description: ISO 4217 code the payment leaves in, e.g. 'EUR'.

target_currency.description: ISO 4217 code the payment must land in, e.g. 'ZAR'.

name: discover_payment
title: Payment Discovery
